title: Impact of Analyst Coverage on Firm Investment

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Method: Instrumental Variables (2SLS)

Why: Analyst coverage (x) is likely endogenous in the investment equation (y) due to omitted variables (e.g., investment opportunities), measurement error, or reverse causality. Broker mergers (z) shift coverage for affected firms but are plausibly unrelated to firm-specific investment shocks, providing exogenous variation in x.

Key assumptions:
- Relevance: Broker mergers affect analyst coverage, Cov(z, x | controls) ≠ 0. Test via first-stage coefficient and F-statistic.
- Exclusion: Broker mergers affect investment only through coverage (no direct effect on y other than via x, conditional on controls).
- Independence: Conditional on controls (firm size/industry/past performance), z is as-if random with respect to potential outcomes.
- Monotonicity: The effect of a broker merger on coverage moves in the same direction for all firms (no defiers). With a binary z, 2SLS identifies the LATE for compliers.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code that:
# - Reads the CSV file from the path provided
# - Runs the appropriate causal analysis
# - Prints a clear numerical result (coefficient, CAR, etc.)
# - Includes basic robustness checks

# Package setup
pkgs <- c("AER", "sandwich", "lmtest")
for (p in pkgs) {
  if (!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages(p, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
  }
}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(AER)
  library(sandwich)
  library(lmtest)
})

# Read data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s71_data.csv")

# Ensure numeric types
df$y <- as.numeric(df$y)
df$x <- as.numeric(df$x)
df$z <- as.numeric(df$z)
df$controls <- as.numeric(df$controls)

# Helper to extract robust coefficient info
extract_coef <- function(model, var = "x") {
  vc <- sandwich::vcovHC(model, type = "HC1")
  ct <- lmtest::coeftest(model, vcov = vc)
  if (!(var %in% rownames(ct))) stop(paste("Variable", var, "not in model."))
  beta <- as.numeric(ct[var, 1])
  se   <- as.numeric(ct[var, 2])
  tval <- as.numeric(ct[var, 3])
  pval <- as.numeric(ct[var, 4])
  dfre <- model$df.residual
  crit <- qt(0.975, dfre)
  ci_l <- beta - crit*se
  ci_u <- beta + crit*se
  list(beta = beta, se = se, t = tval, p = pval, ci_l = ci_l, ci_u = ci_u, df = dfre)
}

# Baseline OLS (for comparison)
ols <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = df)
ols_out <- extract_coef(ols, "x")

# Baseline IV (2SLS): y ~ x + controls, instrumenting x with z
iv_baseline <- AER::ivreg(y ~ x + controls | controls + z, data = df)
iv_out <- extract_coef(iv_baseline, "x")

# First-stage and reduced form
fs <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = df)     # first stage
rf <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = df)     # reduced form

# First-stage: coefficient on z and partial F for z
fs_sum <- summary(fs)
beta_z_fs <- fs_sum$coefficients["z", 1]
se_z_fs   <- fs_sum$coefficients["z", 2]
t_z_fs    <- beta_z_fs / se_z_fs
F_z_fs    <- as.numeric(t_z_fs^2)

# Wald test for z in first stage (partial F vs model without z)
fs_restricted <- lm(x ~ controls, data = df)
wald_fs <- lmtest::waldtest(fs_restricted, fs, test = "F")
F_partial <- tryCatch({
  as.numeric(wald_fs$F[2])
}, error = function(e) NA_real_)

# Reduced-form coefficient on z
rf_sum <- summary(rf)
beta_z_rf <- rf_sum$coefficients["z", 1]
se_z_rf   <- rf_sum$coefficients["z", 2]

# Diagnostics (Wu-Hausman endogeneity test if available)
diag_tab <- tryCatch({
  summary(iv_baseline, diagnostics = TRUE)$diagnostics
}, error = function(e) NULL)
p_endo <- NA
if (!is.null(diag_tab)) {
  rn <- rownames(diag_tab)
  wh_row <- grep("Wu", rn, ignore.case = TRUE)
  if (length(wh_row) > 0 && "p-value" %in% colnames(diag_tab)) {
    p_endo <- as.numeric(diag_tab[wh_row[1], "p-value"])
  }
}

# Robustness 1: IV without controls
iv_noc <- AER::ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = df)
iv_noc_out <- extract_coef(iv_noc, "x")

# Robustness 2: IV with nonlinear control (quadratic term)
iv_quad <- AER::ivreg(y ~ x + controls + I(controls^2) | z + controls + I(controls^2), data = df)
iv_quad_out <- extract_coef(iv_quad, "x")

# Robustness 3: Winsorize 1% tails and re-estimate baseline IV
winsor <- function(v, p = 0.01) {
  lo <- as.numeric(quantile(v, p, na.rm = TRUE, type = 7))
  hi <- as.numeric(quantile(v, 1 - p, na.rm = TRUE, type = 7))
  pmin(pmax(v, lo), hi)
}
df_w <- df
df_w$y <- winsor(df$y, 0.01)
df_w$x <- winsor(df$x, 0.01)
df_w$controls <- winsor(df$controls, 0.01)
iv_w <- AER::ivreg(y ~ x + controls | controls + z, data = df_w)
iv_w_out <- extract_coef(iv_w, "x")

# Print clear numerical results
cat("Main 2SLS estimate (y on analyst coverage x):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Beta_IV = %.4f, SE_robust = %.4f, 95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f], p = %.4f\n",
            iv_out$beta, iv_out$se, iv_out$ci_l, iv_out$ci_u, iv_out$p))
cat("\nDiagnostics and comparisons:\n")
cat(sprintf("  OLS beta (y~x+controls): %.4f (SE_robust = %.4f), p = %.4f\n",
            ols_out$beta, ols_out$se, ols_out$p))
cat(sprintf("  First-stage: coef(z -> x) = %.4f (SE = %.4f), t = %.2f\n",
            beta_z_fs, se_z_fs, t_z_fs))
cat(sprintf("  First-stage partial F for z (given controls): %.2f\n",
            ifelse(is.na(F_partial), F_z_fs, F_partial)))
cat(sprintf("  Reduced form: coef(z -> y) = %.4f (SE = %.4f)\n",
            beta_z_rf, se_z_rf))
if (!is.na(p_endo)) {
  cat(sprintf("  Wu-Hausman endogeneity test p-value: %.4f\n", p_endo))
}

cat("\nRobustness checks (2SLS coefficients on x):\n")
cat(sprintf("  IV without controls: Beta = %.4f, SE = %.4f, p = %.4f\n",
            iv_noc_out$beta, iv_noc_out$se, iv_noc_out$p))
cat(sprintf("  IV with quadratic control: Beta = %.4f, SE = %.4f, p = %.4f\n",
            iv_quad_out$beta, iv_quad_out$se, iv_quad_out$p))
cat(sprintf("  IV with 1%% winsorization: Beta = %.4f, SE = %.4f, p = %.4f\n",
            iv_w_out$beta, iv_w_out$se, iv_w_out$p))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive 2SLS effect of analyst coverage on investment. Broker mergers typically reduce coverage (negative first stage), so the reduced form z → y should be negative if coverage raises investment.
- Magnitude: With standardized-like variables in the preview, a plausible elasticity/slope is in the 0.3–0.8 range for the 2SLS coefficient on x, smaller than or different from OLS if endogeneity biases OLS toward zero or upward.
- Diagnostics: Expect a strong first-stage (F > 10). If endogeneity is material, Wu-Hausman should reject OLS in favor of IV. Robustness checks should yield similar positive estimates.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use broker mergers as an instrument for analyst coverage.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Increased analyst coverage significantly boosts firm investment.
